# Rokib Al Dhin Raadh

> Rokib Al Dhin Raadh is the founder and CEO of OXIEDO and the author of ORMAS, a self-correcting neural network architecture that records what each of its components learned during training. The ORMAS stability result, "Self-Repair as a Bounded Disturbance: Input-to-State Stability of Neural Network Training Dynamics", was accepted after double-blind review for poster presentation at DeepMath 2026 (Conference on the Mathematical Theory of Deep Neural Networks, Ohio State University, 29–30 October 2026). He is 18 and based in Dhaka, Bangladesh.

Website: https://www.raadh.me/ · Company: https://oxiedo.com · Contact: raadxbusiness9@gmail.com

## Key facts

- **Roles:** Founder & CEO, OXIEDO (founded 2023); independent AI researcher; programme committee member, NeurIPS 2026 Trustworthy AI for Good workshop.
- **Research, ORMAS:** a three-signal training architecture: global backpropagation, a per-node local loss through a shared bottleneck readout, and health-gated autonomous self-correction. It detects structural failures during training, repairs them without stopping, and logs every correction with its cause.
- **Headline result:** after a trained convolutional layer is destroyed mid-training (CIFAR-10, three seeds), ORMAS recovers to 80.3% accuracy while a parameter-matched baseline stays at chance (10.0%): a +70.3 percentage-point gap.
- **Other results:** 94.6% task retention versus 47.3% for ResNet-18 in sequential learning; 58.8% zero-shot compositional accuracy (25% chance); 2.5pp versus 7.8pp accuracy decay under 40% label noise.
- **Evidence base:** 383 controlled experiments across four architectures (FC-DAG, CNN, Fat CNN, ResNet-18) on a single RTX 3090; 16,316 lines of PyTorch; every run reproducible from seed.
- **Theory:** the first formal local stability characterization of a self-correcting neural architecture, adapted from Sontag's Input-to-State Stability framework. Accepted at DeepMath 2026; DeepMath publishes no proceedings.
- **Company, OXIEDO:** licenses ORMAS on-premise to regulated industries (AI training, regulated finance, medical AI, data obligation, defence) so institutions can train on data they cannot currently use, with an auditable training record relevant to SR 26-2 model-risk guidance and the EU AI Act high-risk obligations from December 2027. Pre-revenue.
- **Earlier work:** OXIMO, a 40,933-line multi-agent operating system with 2,069 passing tests; Black Bloxie LTD (incorporated in England & Wales on 11 September 2025), a twelve-month controlled field study of OXIMO on a live e-commerce company; five ventures between ages 12 and 17, including a stock-prediction system sold for about $10,000 at 15.
- **Recognition (2026):** DeepMath 2026 paper accepted (poster); NeurIPS 2026 workshop programme committee; Cohere Labs Open Science Community member; IARCO 2026 finalist; ranked highest in the Cosmos Institute grant cycle; accepted by Freshmango and 1752vc Ignite; in the Antler programme process until it was paused over Australian work-permit logistics; Entrepreneur First The Bridge final selection round.

## Scope and limitations

- The stability result is local, not global; global convergence remains open. Review by control theorists is pending.
- Results are on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 with CNN, ResNet and DAG architectures; transformers are a stated next step, not a demonstrated result.
- A two-layer lesion on CIFAR-100 recovers only 7.4%.
- GlassBox telemetry is structural, not semantic, interpretability.

## Frequently asked

- **Who is Rokib Al Dhin Raadh?** Founder and CEO of OXIEDO and author of the ORMAS self-correcting neural network architecture, based in Dhaka, Bangladesh.
- **What is ORMAS?** A neural network architecture that identifies, repairs and records its own failing components during training, instead of relying on post-hoc interpretability.
- **Is the work peer reviewed?** The stability result was accepted after double-blind review at DeepMath 2026 (poster). The full ORMAS paper is a public preprint on Zenodo (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21730363).
- **What does OXIEDO sell?** One on-premise annual licence for ORMAS, with the Model Change Record (a tamper-evident log of every weight change in a training run) as the lead product.
